sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Newcastle's Clean Air Zone does not charge private cars. The Newcastle and Gateshead Clean Air Zone began on 30 January 2023 with charges for non-compliant taxis, buses, coaches and HGVs, and added non-compliant vans at £12.50 a day from 17 July 2023. Private cars are not charged [4]. A grants scheme for affected businesses closed on 30 January 2026, after more than £5.5 million had gone to over 1,100 businesses, tradespeople and taxi drivers [6].

The council has also tried to change the centre's streets. In January 2020 it proposed making Blackett Street traffic-free and re-routing buses, with new delivery and servicing arrangements on Northumberland Street, Grey Street and others [0]. In March 2022 its Cabinet was due to review feedback on pedestrianising Blackett Street, New Bridge Street West and northern Pilgrim Street, and the page we found reports no final decision [3]. Pilgrim Street improvement works included a two-way cycle lane, with vehicles northbound only from 31 July 2023 and completion scheduled for summer 2024 [16]. Improvements to Gallowgate and Percy Street were due to begin in 2026, with Eldon Square Bus Station to close for resurfacing from 10 to 29 June [17].

Parking charges have moved the other way. In July 2022, after about 650 objections, the council amended its proposals so that charges would run to 7pm, not 10pm, in city-centre car parks and on-street bays, with Sunday parking at standard hourly rates instead of a £3 fixed charge. The page links this to the withdrawal of 'Alive after Five' funding, which had allowed free parking from 5pm to 10pm [8]. In January 2024 it proposed raising rates from April 2024, by 20p an hour in the zone and on all on-street bays and 10p outside [9]. Permit fees rose on 3 August 2026, with the first resident permit going from £25 to £35 and city-centre resident annual permits from £500 to £550 [14].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The council's multi-storey car parks are now open for longer. A consultation in September 2025 proposed keeping Grainger Town and Dean Street open 24 hours at weekends, with a 50p-an-hour charge from 7pm to midnight on Fridays and Saturdays [13]. The council's charges table of November 2025 shows both in place [13]. The same table lists seven car parks and their hourly rates: Eldon Square £2.90 an hour, Eldon Garden £2.60 or £13 fixed, Dean Street and Ellison Place £2.30, Grainger Town £1.70 or £11 fixed, St Georges £1.50 and Manors £1.40 or £10 fixed [10][11]. Eldon Square and Eldon Garden are free from 7pm to 8am [10]. The table also records charging points at five multi-storey car parks, with two to five each [24].

Park-and-ride is run through the Metro. Travel North East charges a flat £1.80 a day at its Metro car parks from 6am to 5pm Monday to Saturday, with free parking after 5pm and all day Sunday [21]. At Callerton Parkway, Newcastle Airport has opened a free 'Airport Waiting Zone' for up to 90 minutes of pick-ups, with a free shuttle bus planned to start on 6 January 2026 [22]. For match days Newcastle United says there are no unreserved public car parks at St James' Park, and it recommends public transport and a park and ride from the MetroCentre [25]. We found no sourced figures on a shift from the centre to shopping centres.

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Our Newcastle data cover ten car parks with 2,799 spaces, seven priced in the council's off-street charges table and three Metro lots: Bank Foot (62 spaces), Callerton Parkway (192) and Regent Centre Interchange (183). Five are within 500 m of Grey's Monument (1,813 spaces) and two more within 1 km (549). The council's rates run from £1.40 to £2.90 an hour [10][11], and the Metro lots charge £1.80 a day [21].

Occupancy over August to early October 2026 was low, averaging 20% on weekdays and 16% at weekends. The fullest are Callerton Parkway (28% on weekdays), Manors and Dean Street (both 26%) and Ellison Place (24%). The emptiest are Regent Centre (10%), Grainger Town (14%), and Bank Foot and Eldon Square (both 17%). Eldon Square is the one car park that is busier at weekends (31%, against 17% on weekdays). Within 500 m of the centre the average is 22%, against 15% for the two car parks 500 m to 1 km away. Capacities in our feed differ slightly from the council's table, for example Ellison Place at 126 spaces against 119 and Grainger Town at 410 against 401. The data cover the summer holidays, so term-time figures may differ, and we have no multi-year history for Newcastle.
